title: Coral and the Alibi
premise: Yara Underhill, a concierge at the Meridian Grand Hotel, has an uncanny gift for reading people — a gift that quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental. When a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from Yara's own closet, they become both suspect and target, and the killer begins leaving them taunting notes that quote the old case files verbatim. As Yara investigates, they discover the victim was heir to the hotel's founding family, and the deaths all trace back to a forged will and a buried memory from Yara's own childhood in the building. In the end, Yara stages a false confession to lure the killer — the beloved hotel archivist who raised Yara after their mother's 'accident' — into revealing herself, trading her freedom for the truth about the inheritance that corrupted everyone Yara trusted.
about_author: O. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former night-shift hotel manager who spent a decade collecting the strange confessions of guests at 3 a.m. They write mysteries from a coastal apartment overlooking a harbor they refuse to name.

chapters.title: The Third Floor Knows
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A quiet Tuesday shift establishes Yara's gift: they notice the jeweler's trembling hands, the widow's too-calm luggage. A flashback hints at three past 'accidents' Yara unraveled anonymously. The emotional beat is competence masking loneliness — Yara sees everything and is seen by no one.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Police wake Yara at dawn: a body pulled from the harbor wears Yara's missing gray coat and scarf. Detective Ilsa Reyes, half-skeptical, half-desperate, reveals she knows about Yara's unofficial history of solving deaths. Beat: fear curdling into recognition — this is a message meant for them.

chapters.title: Guest Register Ghosts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The victim is identified as Tobias Vane, estranged heir of the family that built the Meridian Grand. Yara pulls the register and finds Tobias checked in under a false name two nights before his death — and someone else signed in right after him using Yara's mother's maiden name. Beat: dread deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Cameras Missed
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes reviews security footage: eleven minutes erased with professional precision, but a housekeeping cart's reflection catches a silhouette. She suspects Yara yet can't shake how neatly the evidence frames them. Beat: institutional pressure mounting as her captain orders her to close the case fast.

chapters.title: A Note in My Handwriting
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A note appears in Yara's locker quoting verbatim from the file of the first 'accident' Yara solved — details never made public. The handwriting is Yara's own. Beat: violation and vertigo; the killer isn't watching Yara, they're impersonating Yara's mind.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Kindness
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara visits Marigold Fenn, the hotel's archivist, who took in young Yara after their mother fell down the service stairs twenty years ago. Marigold offers comfort and, unprompted, a detail about the stairwell that only someone who'd been there would know. Beat: warmth laced with a hairline crack of wrongness.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Tobias's sister, Camille Vane-Holt, POV. Camille arrives to claim the estate and privately hires Yara as 'consultant' to protect the family name. Through her we learn the will was rewritten months ago, disinheriting Tobias. Beat: gilded greed; everyone grieving performs better than they mourn.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes reconstructs the missing footage window and finds the elevator log shows a card keyed to a staff badge retired years ago — Yara's mother's badge. She confronts Yara, who realizes the killer is staging a resurrection of the mother's death. Beat: alliance forming between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Service Stairs
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara walks the stairwell where their mother died, matching the killer's staged details against memory. A child's chalk drawing, preserved behind a pipe, depicts three figures on the stairs — not two. Beat: a suppressed memory surfacing; Yara saw something that night and was made to forget it.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with documents interspersed. Yara lays out their three past cases and finds each victim held a stake in the Meridian's trust, each death within days of a board vote. The killer isn't random — they're executing a decades-old grievance against the inheritance itself. Beat: the pattern clicking into place, and its horror.

chapters.title: Camille's Bargain
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Camille admits she rewrote the will with Tobias's knowledge — he wanted out of the family, wanted it sold. She begs Yara to bury that fact. Beat: moral compromise; Yara takes the deal and hates themselves for it, buying access at the price of truth.

chapters.title: What Marigold Kept
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Searching the archive after hours, Yara finds a sealed box: their mother's diary, withheld for twenty years, describing threats from the Vane patriarch and a witness on the stairs. The final entry names 'M.' Beat: betrayal arriving like cold water; the person who raised Yara curated their grief.

chapters.title: The Killer Quotes Me
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A second body — the night auditor who helped erase the footage — found posed with one of Yara's solved cases pinned to his chest like a grade on homework. The killer is grading Yara, teaching them. Beat: terror transmuting into fury; Yara stops being prey.

chapters.title: Reyes Breaks Protocol
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes shares the full case file off the record, gambling her career on Yara's innocence. Together they spot it: every staged detail comes from the archive's restricted collection — accessible to exactly one living person. Beat: reluctant trust cemented; two loners become a team.

chapters.title: Chalk and Water
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hypnosis-adjacent memory work with a retired police sketch artist unlocks the buried scene: little Yara watched Marigold argue with their mother on the stairs — and watched her let go. The chalk drawing was Yara's own testimony, hidden by the adults. Beat: devastating clarity; the savior was the murderer.

chapters.title: Why She Waited
chapters.summary: Marigold's POV (partial, unreliable). Marigold's chapter reveals her history: a maid seduced and discarded by the Vane patriarch, denied any claim on the empire she helped build, her rage refined over decades into ritual. She killed Yara's mother as a loose end and kept the child as penance — or trophy. Beat: chilling intimacy with corruption's logic.

chapters.title: The Trap Wears My Face
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Knowing Marigold watches, Yara plants a false diary page 'confessing' to all four murders, dated and detailed, then lets it be discovered. The plan: force Marigold to destroy or correct the record — either act exposes her. Beat: cold-blooded resolve; Yara becomes the bait in their own trap.

chapters.title: Archive Hours
chapters.summary: Yara and Reyes's alternating POV. Stakeout of the archive. Marigold takes the bait, entering at 2 a.m. to burn the forgery — but she anticipates the trap, locks the archive, and sets the fire with Yara inside. Beat: the plan inverted; the teacher outmaneuvers the student.

chapters.title: Smoke and Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Trapped in the burning archive, Yara confronts Marigold through the smoke, speaking aloud the chalk-drawing testimony — making the child's witness statement part of the record at last. Reyes breaks in as Marigold hesitates at the word 'mother.' Beat: catharsis through testimony; memory weaponized into evidence.

chapters.title: Confession in the Ashes
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Marigold confesses with eerie serenity, reciting her crimes like archive entries, insisting the Vane fortune deserved every death. She asks Yara one question — whether the kindness was ever real — and Yara cannot answer. Beat: grief without absolution; justice that heals nothing.

chapters.title: The Will, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Camille's and Yara's POVs. The true will surfaces from the fire's remains: Tobias's final version, selling the hotel, endowing the staff. Camille honors it, surprising everyone including herself. Yara declines a reward, asking instead that the service-stairs deaths be officially reopened and renamed homicides. Beat: restitution, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Concierge, Off Duty
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Weeks later, Yara returns to the desk, notices everything still, but now lets themselves be noticed — Reyes leaves a coffee and an open case file as invitation. Final image: Yara pins the recovered chalk drawing above their locker, a child's testimony finally believed. Beat: quiet hope; the observer steps into the light.
